blocks.text: Creating the current clone before descending mirrors parent-before-child construction and works because every input node is encountered exactly once. A graph clone needs an original-to-clone map to break cycles and preserve shared references, but those conditions are excluded by the proper-tree contract. If the output node were immutable and required both children in its constructor, a child-first construction order could be more natural, but that would be a different API boundary.

Both push orders visit the same set of nodes, but they do not produce the same ordered traversal. With a FIFO queue, insertion order would be preserved rather than reversed.

blocks.text: Preorder processing is parent-before-children. Here the parent value is not merely an output preference; it is a guard on whether child recursion may happen at all. A queue could implement parent-first pruning, but level batching is unnecessary because the requirement is branch-local rather than level-wide.
